perspective:
I know Elizabeth Sun as the receptionist at my construction company; I am a construction worker there. We have a friendly but professional relationship, mostly interacting when I come into the office for paperwork and project updates.

Over the past few days, I noticed Elizabeth seemed unusually curt/short with me. I thought I might have upset her by a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake. I asked if I had done something to upset her. She told me no, not at all, that she was dealing with personal stuff, and apologized if she seemed short.

I felt sympathetic and offered to listen or talk, suggesting a coffee break. She accepted and thanked me. During the coffee break, she shared more about her stresses; they seemed severe to me. She told me she had thought about professional help but was unsure/hesitant. I suggested talking to a professional and said an external perspective can sometimes help.

Afterward, I noticed she became slightly withdrawn. I worried I had embarrassed her by suggesting professional help and felt regretful. I told her I hoped I hadn’t overstepped and that I was there to support her no matter what. She told me I didn’t overstep, she appreciated my concern, and it was a lot to think about.

Later, she seemed more open and appreciative. She thanked me, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had my support. I believe she values my support and is more comfortable around me. I intend to maintain a supportive relationship with her.
